title: The Feminine Mystique

vibeProfile.oneLine: Naming the quiet despair of the mid-century American housewife.

summary: Betty Friedan gave a name to 'the problem that has no name': the stifled unhappiness of educated American women confined to suburban homemaking in the 1950s. Drawing on interviews and her own experience, she argued that a whole society had told women their only fulfilment lay in husband, children and house, and that the resulting emptiness was real and widespread. The book helped ignite second-wave feminism and remains a landmark of postwar social criticism.
whyReadIt: The book that lit the fuse of second-wave feminism, by naming a quiet, widespread despair. A landmark of social criticism.

funFacts.text: Friedan went on to co-found the National Organization for Women in 1966.
